title: Lakeview Inference runway + reliability playbook sync
summary: Monthly health/check-in focused on usage spike mitigation, cost drivers, and preparing a reliability playbook for next quarter. Discussed Dedicated vs Hosted routing for peak windows, VPC options, and a short benchmarking plan.
topics: recent usage spike and burst patterns
action_items: Sofia - share last 30 days of env configs and traffic p95 by route - due 2027-05-03
Devon - run latency + cost microbench for their prompt set and share spreadsheet - due 2027-05-05
Maya - send pricing comps and Dedicated capacity options - due 2027-04-30
next_steps: Redwood to run a 24h bench on customer's peak prompt set (Devon)
Customer to share anonymized traffic CSVs and example prompts (Sofia)
Schedule architecture deep-dive next week to discuss VPC/KMS integration (Evan + Devon)
Follow up with SOC2 & audit docs link
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-04-28
Start time: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Devon Patel (Redwood SE), Rajat Singh (Lakeview Head of ML), Sofia Martinez (Lakeview Platform Eng Manager), Evan Lee (Lakeview CTO)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on, we wanted to keep this tight, 60 minutes ish, go over the spike you had last week and lay out a reliability playbook for the next quarter.
[00:18] Rajat: Yeah thanks Maya, appreciate it. We had a pretty big spike on Tuesday night — about 3x baseline for ~45 minutes — and some tail latency issues. Not sure if it was batching or a cache miss.
[00:36] Devon: Got it. Can you share the route names and whether those were single-shot calls or chat streams? Sometimes streaming vs non-streaming changes the kv cache behavior.
[00:49] Sofia: Mostly single-shot generation for our summarization endpoint, a small percentage streamed. We send multi-turn context but we flush parts of the context out very often because of privacy rules.
[01:05] Maya: Quick qual question — are you on Hosted or are you already using Dedicated capacity for any traffic?
[01:12] Evan: We're mixed. Most production is on Hosted but we put a couple of heavy routes on a Dedicated pool last month. The spike hit the Hosted side.
[01:22] Devon: Okay that explains it; hosted pools can burst but competing tenants at that window may cause queuing. We can look at routing policy to push those high-p95 routes to Dedicated during expected peaks.
[01:35] Rajat: The billing was shocking, our cost went up 2.4x for that window. We need better attribution, token-level breakdown, something we can show execs.
[01:46] Maya: Understood. We'll include a cost breakdown per-route and per-model for the spike window. Devon will run the microbench to estimate per-token economics with and without prefix caching and different batch sizes.
[01:57] Sofia: A question — is Redwood's prefix cache the same as KV cache? I saw it referenced a few ways in the docs and some team members say KB cache.
[02:09] Devon: Yeah reporting inconsistency, our bad. It's KV cache — key-value cache for transformer states. It reduces repeated compute on shared prefixes. But if you flush context or have varying prompts it gives less benefit.
[02:22] Rajat: During the spike we suspect the cache hit rate dropped because of a sudden mix of prompt variants.
[02:29] Devon: That would do it. Also quantization profile could impact latency; if you're on a quantized model variant the kernel selection may change p95.
[02:40] Sofia: Kwantization?
[02:42] Devon: (laughs) quantization, yeah sorry, speech to text in my head.
[02:47] Maya: No worries. We should talk about fallback policies — if Dedicated is saturated, we can route to a cheaper variant with graceful degradation. That preserves availability.
[03:01] Evan: We care more about correctness than raw perf for some routes — e.g., compliance checks — but for customer-facing recs we prefer lower latency.
[03:12] Rajat: Also curious on private deployment. If we move critical routes into a VPC or on-prem, can we keep the same console and rollouts?
[03:23] Maya: Yes, Redwood Private retains the same control plane UI and rollout semantics. The difference is the control plane is in your VPC and you control the KMS keys. Audit logs and retention can be tuned.
[03:36] Sofia: SOC2 and third-party audit docs — can you resend? I couldn't find the latest in the portal.
[03:44] Maya: I'll send the SOC2 and penetration test summary after this call.
[03:48] Devon: For the bench plan — we'll run a 24 hour bench on a copy of your peak traffic shape. We'll measure p50/p95/p99, cost/token, and cache hit rates. We'll also test 3 policies: all-hosted, mixed-hosted-with-priority-routing, and Dedicated-heavy.
[04:06] Rajat: Sounds good. A practical constraint — we have to keep PII out of anything we share. We'll provide anonymized prompts and an aggregate traffic CSV.
[04:18] Maya: Perfect, that works. For next steps I'll send a pricing adj sheet and options for reserved Dedicated capacity — monthly and annual.
[04:29] Evan: One more question — can Redwood's console show token-level cost allocation by team or route? That would make chargebacks much easier.
[04:40] Devon: We have per-route cost breakdown in Console today, token-level per-route is a new view we'll enable as part of the Optimize feature rollout. I can show a prototype in the deep-dive.
[04:53] Sofia: If you can take our route list and map to those views, that would help our finance team sign off.
[04:59] Maya: We'll include example screenshots and an export for finance.
[05:05] Rajat: Also, can we set up a runbook for on-call? When latency spikes happen, who should be paged and what immediate actions do we take — like redirecting a route to Dedicated or toggling caching?
[05:19] Devon: We'll draft a playbook: detection thresholds (p95 > X ms for Y minutes), triggering automated routing to Dedicated, and manual steps. We'll also recommend autoscale buffer sizes.
[05:31] Evan: We're concerned about KMS/HSM integration timeline — our security team wants it in place before any dedicated pilot.
[05:39] Maya: KMS integration is supported; latency to integrate depends on your key rotation policies. We'll include integration checklist.
[05:46] Sophia: (overlap) it's Sofia — small correction, we rotate keys monthly.
[05:51] Devon: That helps, we'll note the rotation schedule for the checklist.
[05:55] Maya: Ok let's recap and set owners.
[06:02] (Recap) Maya: Action items — Sofia share anonymized traffic and prompt set; Devon run bench and produce spreadsheet; Maya send pricing, SOC2, and playbook draft. We'll schedule architecture deep-dive next Tue.
[06:20] Rajat: Thanks, appreciate the quick turnaround.
[06:24] Evan: Thanks all.

(Transcript notes: occasional transcription errors around technical terms — e.g., "KV cache" sometimes appears as "K B cache" or "prefix cache"; speaker labels auto-assigned in spots.)
